   - Start oral antibiotic: Trimethoprim or Nitrofurantoin for 3 days (specific agent/dose/route/frequency not documented).

Assessment & Plan:
1. Dysuria, urinary frequency, suprapubic pain with possible hematuria:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Acute uncomplicated bacterial cystitis. Supported by DDx: “Acute uncomplicated bacterial cystitis” (High likelihood) — consistent with dysuria, frequency, suprapubic aching worse with voiding, and pink urine; absence of fever/flank pain argues against upper tract involvement.
   - Differential diagnosis (from DDx, consistent with transcript):
     • Urethritis due to STI (Medium): sexually active without condoms; less typical given hematuria and no discharge.  
     • Urolithiasis (Low): hematuria possible; lacks colicky flank pain/radiation.  
     • Chemical/irritant urethritis (Low): no exposure history; hematuria less typical.  
     • Bladder pain syndrome/interstitial cystitis (Low): acute presentation not typical.
   - Investigations planned: Midstream urine for dipstick and culture/sensitivity (arranged); clinic to inform results and tailor therapy.
   - Treatment planned: Start oral antibiotic — Trimethoprim or Nitrofurantoin for 3 days (specific agent/dose/route/frequency not documented); increase fluids; Paracetamol (acetaminophen) as needed.
   - Relevant referrals: None.
2. Cannabis use (one-time trial) and counseling:

   - Differential diagnosis: Not applicable.
   - Investigations planned: None.
   - Treatment planned: Advice to avoid ongoing use.
